terms.gloss: a lead bullet; classically a sling bullet
evidence: Caes. BG 5.43.1 (Lewis & Short s.v. glāns: “an acorn-shaped ball of lead or clay which was hurled at the enemy”)
terms.comment: Glāns, an acorn, was the acorn-shaped shot of lead or clay hurled from a sling; Traupman gives the phrase for a modern bullet. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

sources: Lewis & Short: glans
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 284.
